Q: When should I use reinterpret_cast? A:

First, you have some data in a specific type like int here:

int x = 0x7FFFFFFF: // ==nan in binary representation

Then you want to access the same variable as an other type like float: You can decide between

float y = reinterpret_cast<float&>(x);

// This could only be used in C++. It looks like a function with template-parameters

or

float y = *(float*)&(x);

// This could be used in C and C++

BRIEF: It means that the same memory is used as a different type. So you could convert binary representations of floats as int type like above to floats. 0x80000000 is -0 for example (the mantissa and exponent are null but the sign, the MSb, is one. This also works for doubles and long doubles.

OPTIMIZE: I think reinterpret_cast would be optimized in many compilers, while the C casting is made by pointerarithmetic (the value must be copied to the memory, because pointers couldn't point to CPU registers).

NOTE: In both cases you should save the cast value in a variable before cast! This macro could help:

#define asvar(x) ({decltype(x) __tmp__ = (x); __tmp__; })

Q: Recommend a book for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP and MySQL A:

A single book wouldn't cut it as it is too much info to pack into a single volume. However, for PHP and MySQL try the Larry Ullman books. (there are 3) or PHP and MySQL by Jon Duckett.

For HTML, CSS and JavaScript try Jennifer Robins': Learning Web Design: A Beginner's Guide to HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Web Images. Sixth Edition.

Q: How to implement logging of all changes mysql database? A:

MySQL's Binary Log does exactly that.

This auditing would occur at the system level, outside of the scope of the database.

Binary Log

The Binary Log is saved as numbered log files to /var/lib/mysql/binlog_.xxxx, and it may be used for examining the outcomes of SQL statements or doing point-in-time restoration.

mysqlbinlog -v /var/lib/mysql/binlog.xxxx

### DELETE FROM `test`.`Sessions`
### WHERE
###   @1=3
###   @2='TestSessionExpiration'
###   @3='2026-04-26 22:36:26.338604'

The verbose option, -v, has mysqlbinlog reconstruct and print an approximation of the queries from the encoded log file.

Here, the WHERE clause shows the values of the actual row affected, not the query executed. Very very handy.

General Query Log

If you enable the General Query Log in /etc/mysql/my.cnf, you can really get a full picture of the queries being run and the outcomes.

[mysqld]
general_log_file        = /var/log/mysql/mysql.log
general_log             = 1

This shows the statements being executed, along with the timestamp and connection ID:

2026-04-26T22:56:59.664958Z    43 Execute    DELETE FROM Sessions WHERE Expires <= '2026-04-26 22:56:59.661578'

This technique was helpful for debugging sub-millisecond execution times for queries in Goroutines with wake up timers.

Application layer information like IP addresses is probably going to require a solution with triggers. This would also allow you to query the information from the application.

MySQL Reference Manual

  • The Binary Log File
  • mysqlbinlog Row Event Display
  • The General Query Log

Q: Using reinterpret_cast to check inheritance at compile time A:

You're trying to solve a problem that doesn't need to be solved. Since C++11, we have type traits that allow us to check things like this explicitly in template metaprogramming.

For example, is_base_of.

Q: Understanding the SIMD shuffle control mask A:

mask isn't an AND mask. The shuffle-control vector elements are indices into the concatenation of the source vectors. Each result element is basically the result of res[i] = ab[ mask[i] ].

SIMD shuffles are parallel table-lookups, where the the control vector (called "mask" for short, for some reason) is a vector of indices and the other 1 or 2 inputs are the table. (Some instructions only take one source vector of data. Some like x86 SSE2 shufps only let any given index access one of the two source vectors. Some like AVX-512 vterm2d are like the GCC generic builtin, indexing the concatenation of two vectors. PowerPC also has a byte shuffle like that.)

Related: Convert _mm_shuffle_epi32 to C expression for the permutation? shows a plain C equivalent for _mm_shuffle_epi32 (pshufd) with compile-time-constant indices. You have a 2-input shuffle that indexes into the concatenation of a and b (in that order).

AVX1/AVX2 doesn't have a shuffle that actually does this for runtime-variable inputs, so that __builtin_shuffle would have to compile to multiple instructions.

AVX512F vpermt2d works exactly this way, though.
